veranderings.blok: Energie wat van ver af kom
veranderings.voor: kry die lig teen die kombuis se dak
veranderings.na: kry die lig aan die kombuis se plafon
veranderings.rede: Indoors a light hangs from the ceiling (plafon); 'dak' is the roof, and 'aan' fits a fitting that hangs better than 'teen'.

veranderings.blok: Energie wat van ver af kom
veranderings.voor: sy energie nie daar naby nie
veranderings.na: sy energie nie van naby af nie
veranderings.rede: 'kry ... nie daar naby nie' lacks the source preposition; 'nie van naby af nie' is the natural idiom.

veranderings.blok: Energie wat van ver af kom
veranderings.na: oor 'n pad wat kilometers lank is
veranderings.rede: 'n pad van kilometers ver' is an awkward construction; a route is described as long, not far.

veranderings.voor: ver genoeg terug en jy kom
veranderings.na: ver genoeg terug, en jy kom
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two complete sentences here (an imperative and 'jy kom ... uit'), so a comma goes before it.
As a conjunction introducing a clause, standard written Afrikaans uses 'totdat' rather than 'tot'.

veranderings.blok: Wat die stasie met die steenkool doen
veranderings.rede: In written study text a thing (the machine) is referred to as 'dit', not the colloquial 'hom'.

veranderings.blok: Nie elke stasie brand steenkool nie
veranderings.rede: This is the first machine mentioned at the dam station, so the indefinite article fits, as in the block's last sentence and the glossary.

veranderings.blok: Nie elke stasie brand steenkool nie
veranderings.voor: brand niks en die vallende water
veranderings.na: brand niks nie, en die vallende water
veranderings.rede: Afrikaans needs the closing 'nie' after 'niks' in this clause, and AWS 2017 puts a comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have a subject and verb.

vlae.blok: Nie elke stasie brand steenkool nie
vlae.teks: 'n Kernkragstasie brand ook nie steenkool nie en kry sy hitte uit kernkrag.
vlae.rede: 'kernkrag' uses 'krag' where the lesson otherwise insists on 'energie' (see the protected entry for energie/krag), and the sentence explains the station's heat by its own name; changing it to 'kernenergie' would alter a subject term, so this is for the writer or a person to decide, not a language edit.
